Who Should Attend

Business Process Improvement Executive
Account Operations Analyst
Transaction Banking Operations Analyst
Client Service Officer / Client Support Service Officer
What's In It for Me
Demystify GenAI: Move beyond the hype to understand the actual mechanics of LLMs and how they apply specifically to banking, insurance, and wealth management.
Master Prompt Engineering: Learn the CRAFT framework to move from vague queries to high-precision outputs that meet professional financial standards.
Optimize Your Workflow: Use the 3A Framework to audit your daily tasks and identify high-value opportunities to automate repetitive work or augment complex analysis.
Govern Your Outputs: Gain the critical evaluation skills needed to supervise AI tools effectively, using the VERIFY and FEAT frameworks to manage risks like hallucinations and bias while remaining compliant with MAS guidelines.
Course Overview
This is a 1-day instructor-led workshop designed for financial services professionals who need to move from passive awareness to operational implementation of AI.
Unlike general AI courses, this program is contextualized for the unique constraints of the financial sector. The journey moves rapidly from Foundations (GenAI vs. ML) to Execution (CRAFT Prompting) to Optimization (Workflow Mapping) and finally to Supervision (Critical Evaluation and Ethics). The program culminates in a practical assessment where learners demonstrate their ability to implement AI tools within a regulated business environment.

Course Objectives
Explain core AI concepts (AI, ML, GenAI) and their applications in financial services.
Apply the CRAFT framework to design and iterate effective prompts.
Analyze work instructions using the 3A Framework to identify AI opportunities
Extract process parameters like inputs and constraints from task specifications to guide AI integration
Evaluate AI outputs using the VERIFY framework to detect hallucinations and logic gaps.
Measure effectiveness using metrics like time saved and error reduction.
Implement AI while adhering to FEAT principles and risk management procedures.
Pre-requisites
The admission requirements are:
Diploma or degree
Proficient in the English language
Read, write, and speak English at WPL Level 4
Manipulate numbers at WPN Level 4
Course Outline
Day 1:
Learning Unit 1: GenAI Fundamentals & The Financial Landscape
The AI Tech Spectrum: Defining the hierarchy from Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to the accessibility of Generative AI.
Predictive vs. Generative: Understanding why ML predicts outcomes (e.g., fraud detection) while GenAI creates new content (e.g., reports and emails).
AI in Financial Services Today: Exploring high-value use cases across Risk Management, Operations, Customer Experience, and Trading.
How LLMs Work: Moving from "thinking" to "word prediction" and understanding the training vs. generation phases.
Boundaries & Limitations: Recognizing what GenAI cannot do, including its lack of real-time market data access and confidentiality risks without enterprise versions.
Learning Unit 2: Precision Prompting via the CRAFT Framework
The Anatomy of a Prompt: Moving from vague instructions to structured commands using What, Context, and Format.
The CRAFT Framework: A systematic approach for consistent results using Context, Role, Action, Format, and Tone.
Context & Role Engineering: Setting the professional foundation by defining industry constraints and specific personas (e.g., Senior Relationship Manager).
Precision Execution: Defining actions through clear verbs and specifying structural formats for professional banking outputs.
Prompt Iteration: Mastering the process of evaluating outputs, refining unclear elements, and documenting improvements for team reuse.
Learning Unit 3: Workflow Analysis & AI Integration
The 3A Framework: Deciding when to Automate (repetitive/low complexity), Augment (human-assisted), or Amplify (scaling expertise).
AI Opportunity Identification: Using the Task Suitability Checklist to find "Quick Wins" based on repetition, clear inputs/outputs, and rule-based patterns.
Extracting Process Parameters: Documenting the inputs, outputs, and constraints required to successfully integrate AI into bank-standard workflows (e.g., customer onboarding).
Measuring Effectiveness: Defining the metrics of success, including time saved per task, output quality improvements, and capacity increases.
Red Flags: Identifying tasks that are unsuitable for AI, such as those involving highly confidential data or unique ethical judgments.
Learning Unit 4: Critical Evaluation & Responsible AI (FEAT)
AI Failure Modes: Understanding hallucinations, bias, knowledge cutoffs, and misunderstandings in a financial context.
The VERIFY Framework: Operationalizing a 6-step systematic review to Validate sources, Evaluate logic, Review bias, Investigate numbers, Flag risks, and apply Your expertise.
Responsible AI (FEAT Principles): Implementing the MAS standard of Fairness, Explainability, Accountability, and Transparency in every AI interaction.
Human-in-the-Loop: Understanding personal accountability and the professional responsibility that cannot be delegated to AI.
Escalation Protocols: Identifying mandatory triggers for escalation, including client-facing communications and high-stakes credit or investment decisions.

IBF Funding Eligibility
This course has been accredited under the Skills Framework for Financial Services and is eligible for funding under the IBF Standards Training Scheme (IBF-STS), subject to all eligibility criteria being met.
Participants are advised to assess the suitability of the course and its relevance to his/her business activities or job roles.
The IBF-STS is available to eligible entities and individuals based on the prevalent funding eligibility, quantum and caps. IBF-STS provides up to 70% course fee subsidy support for direct training costs subject to a cap of $3,000 per candidate per course subject to all eligibility criteria being met.
This course also fulfils the following Technical Skills and Competencies TSCs
Generative AI Prompt Engineering (SFW-BAS-0009-0.0), Proficiency Level: Basic
Participants are encouraged to access the IBF MySkills Portfolio to track their training progress and skills acquisition against the Skills Framework for Financial Services. You can apply for IBF Certification after fulfilling the required number of Technical Skills and Competencies (TSCs) for the selected job role. Find out more about IBF certification and the application process.
